text:
marta: Heads-up — ran the GPTQ->AWQ candidate profile on orca-v2-13b using the new per-task routing config. Quick summary: most tasks stable, but a couple of odd deltas we should triage.

marta: Results snapshot: 
- summarization: -0.6% ROUGE (noise)
- codegen (simple algos): -4.8% pass@1 (regression)
- structured legal templates: format error rate +9% (bracket escapes, numbered lists)
- numeric QA: hallucination spike on list outputs (precision loss on trailing digits)

marta: Repro steps (local):
```bash
# run candidate profile
./bench/run_eval --model orca-v2-13b --quant awq-gptq-candidate --suites summarization,codegen,legal,qa --out /tmp/bench.json
```

kenji: can you paste a failing example for the legal template? want to see exact tokenization/linebreak issues.

marta: sure — here's one from legal-template-dev set (original vs quantized):
```
ORIGINAL:
1. Parties: Alice Corp. ("Seller") and Beta LLC ("Buyer").
2. Delivery: Seller shall deliver on or before 2025-10-01.

QUANTIZED:
1. Parties: Alice Corp. (\"Seller\") and Beta LLC (\"Buyer\").2. Delivery: Seller shall deliver on or before 2025 - 10 - 01.
```

marta: Notice the missing newline and added spaces around the date — downstream parsers treat that as two tokens and our structured extractor fails.

sam: thanks — initial look: seems like AWQ packing changed whitespace token boundaries for parentheses and date-like tokens. I re-ran on a small probe set: codegen drop correlates with long-line wrapping in quantized KV cache.

sam: quick numbers from probe (n=200 examples):
- codegen: baseline pass@1 62 -> quant 59
- legal-format errors: baseline 3/200 -> quant 21/200
- numeric QA hallucination (high-confidence wrong numbers): baseline 1 -> quant 7

ci-bench-bot: CI job 8421 finished for profile awq-gptq-candidate. Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/8421/bench.json (sha256: abc123...).

kenji: hypothesis: AWQ per-tensor quant scale locking plus our tokenizer merges produce merged tokens across punctuation that used to be separate. That would explain both newline collapse and numeric tail errors.

ria: can we canary this behind a routing rule (5% traffic to AWQ candidate, fallback to baseline on confidence threshold) while we triage? Product wants a low-risk rollout.

marta: yes — I can create a rollout in console. Proposed config: 5% AWQ, 95% baseline, and confidence cutoff 0.8 on numeric outputs -> fallback to baseline. Anyone object?

kenji: go for it. Meanwhile I'll dump tokenization diffs for the failing examples and try a micro-quant tweak (preserve int8 for punctuation tokens) to see if it closes the gap.

sam: if we can get a short eval set of 500 targeted legal/numeric/code examples, I'll run a focused sweep for quant params and per-workload kernel selection.

marta: I'll assemble the set and upload to s3://redwood-ml/triage/1825001234/ and post the link.

marta: tagging @ria for rollout approval and @kenji for triage priority. :eyes:

ria: approved for canary, add alert on formatting-error-rate > 5% and hallucination-rate > 2% so oncall gets paged.

sam: noted. starting parameter grid tonight and will post quick diff results tomorrow morning.

marta: thanks — keeping this thread for notes and artifacts.
